signature.name: VTask.cycleFactors
signature.type: {α : Type u_2} -> [Fintype α] -> [LinearOrder α] -> (f : Equiv.Perm α) -> { l // l.prod = f ∧ (∀ g ∈ l, g.IsCycle) ∧ List.Pairwise Equiv.Perm.Disjoint l }

conventions.statement: The linear order on α determines the order in which cycles appear in the output list: they are listed by scanning α in ascending order and starting a new cycle at each point not yet accounted for.
conventions.note: The set of cycles is canonical; the list order depends on the LinearOrder instance.

conventions.statement: Fixed points of f (where f(x) = x) contribute no entry to the list, because the identity is not a cycle.
For the identity permutation, the output list is empty, and the empty product equals the identity.
conventions.note: This is the base/boundary case of the construction.

facts.statement: ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [LinearOrder α], ((VTask.cycleFactors (1 : Equiv.Perm α)) : List (Equiv.Perm α)) = []

provenance.note: authored by eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6; unvalidated by the v1.2 kernel validation ladder

facts.statement: ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [LinearOrder α] (f : Equiv.Perm α), (VTask.cycleFactors f : List (Equiv.Perm α)).prod = f

provenance.note: authored by eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6; unvalidated by the v1.2 kernel validation ladder

facts.statement: ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [LinearOrder α] (f : Equiv.Perm α) (g : Equiv.Perm α), g ∈ (VTask.cycleFactors f : List (Equiv.Perm α)) → g.IsCycle

facts.statement: ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [LinearOrder α] (f : Equiv.Perm α), List.Pairwise Equiv.Perm.Disjoint (VTask.cycleFactors f : List (Equiv.Perm α))
